question: Why was salt, rather than bread or milk, chosen to carry iodine into diets?
answer: Because nearly everyone eats a steady few grams a day in every season and class, and it comes from a handful of producers. Dosing a few salt works beats policing thousands of bakers. Switzerland began in 1922; WHO advises 20 to 40 mg of iodine per kilogram of salt. The shaker became a medicine.
move: To reach everyone, pick the thing everyone already uses in the same amount.
reference: WHO, UNICEF & ICCIDD, Assessment of iodine deficiency disorders and monitoring their elimination, 3rd edition, World Health Organization, 2007
